options.text: The fixed amount of water has reached its dissolving limit for copper sulphate under these conditions.
The remaining copper sulphate will dissolve if Yash only stirs longer, with no other change.
Undissolved copper sulphate at the bottom means the water never dissolved any copper sulphate.
A dissolving limit applies only when the water is boiling, not at room temperature.

stem:
Yash adds copper sulphate crystals little by little to a fixed amount of water at room temperature, stirring each time. After several additions, some copper sulphate stays undissolved at the bottom no matter how long he stirs.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Undissolved solute after stirring means the fixed amount of solvent has reached its dissolving limit (solubility) under those conditions.
